source.title: Design target: bounty-funded adventurer economy and expanded Quest Shop
source.body:
## Owner-approved design target — 2026-11-22

**Goal:** Players should be able to pursue a viable *bounty → coins → shop → better-equipped adventuring* career, including a mostly hunting-based playstyle, without mandatory grinding for food, gear, repairs, rare ingredients or random chest loot. Keep crafting, mining, magic and exploration useful alternatives, not compulsory chores. The Quest Shop removes frustration/rare-drop RNG rather than serving only as a cobblestone vendor.

### Decree payout policy — approved

| Decree family | Payout identity | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ordinary/general livelihood decrees** (fishing, farming, culinary, mining, forestry/crafting, etc.) | **Mixed coins and thematic items** | A meaningful mixture of coin-paying and material/item-paying contracts. Do **not** assume every bounty has to grant both at once; honor native Bountiful reward representation and retain useful item alternatives. |
| **Ordinary Hunter's Decree** (`tmm_hunting`, including the starting Inn board) | **Coins only** | Professional monster hunting is a direct earning route. All rewards are Quest Shop team coins, not arrows, leather or unrelated filler. This is the *general hunting decree*, not a rule that requires the player's specialist Hunter Path or that changes any separately defined specialist Hunter decree. |
| **Major magic-school and other specialist decrees** (Iron's, Ars, Occultism, transformations/classes where approved) | **Predominantly thematic materials/items, rarely coins** | The special reason to select an Iron's decree is to earn useful Iron's resources, including inks. Rare coin contracts are allowed but must not crowd out the material identity. Preserve approved existing reward rosters/gates, particularly Occultism's locked selections. |

No numerical coin probabilities, payout amounts or earning rates are locked yet; decide and calibrate using Bountiful's actual supported reward selection/command format and in-game effort. Keep **one shared Quest Shop currency**; do not invent a second bounty coin system. General hunting remains available to non-Hunters. Specialized Path bonuses may make hunting more effective without owning currency/MXP.

### Expanded Quest Shop target — approved direction

- Stock useful **anti-grind resources**: calcite, amethyst, building variants, rare-but-not-gated magical reagents, and all five Iron's ink tiers including high-end inks (price by difficulty).
- Provide the supplies to *live on contracts*: a variety of foods fitting different dietary paths; ordinary weapons, armor, bows, combat consumables, maintenance/repair conveniences, and **specific enchanted books and enchanted gear**.
- Offer **most or all ordinary collectible Artifacts and Relics** individually, with very high prices for exceptional ones. This replaces endless chest RNG with an achievable longer-term bounty goal. Fresh/unlevelled Relics preferred where native mechanics require progression/initialization.
- Treat the previously discussed price bands as **examples**, not approved fixed values. Protect genuinely intended boss/ritual/transformation gates and banned items; normal rarity or power alone should not preclude a shop offer. Evaluate potential ProjectE-specific repair talismans against their actual intended gate rather than automatically selling the gated item.
- Keep existing vanilla ore purchases, board purchase and other approved entries unless separately changed. Avoid a duplicate vendor mod.

**Balance principle:** Shopping costs earned currency; crafting costs materials; exploration costs effort/risk. None should dominate universally. The player should be able to earn enough via normal Hunter contracts to maintain food/equipment, buy upgrades and ultimately purchase a rare Relic without mining/farming/enchanting as mandatory prerequisites.

### Engineering constraints and scoped future work

- Bountiful's current pilot `config/bountiful/bounty_pools/tmm_hunting_rews.json` uses arrows/leather; **that conflicts with this new target** and must be replaced with coin-only payouts when implementing the design. Existing `scripts/compile_bountiful_contracts.py` builds thematic-item payouts and currently rejects direct coin settlement. Coordinate the new payout compilation with the existing Bountiful writer / #365 rather than rewriting its owned runtime from an unrelated branch.
- Quest Shop 1.4.0 entries only support `item`, `amount`, `cost`, `category`: to sell **specific enchanted books, enchanted equipment, initialized component-bearing gear** or other specialized stacks, inspect/extend supported item-component serialization or add a narrow compatible purchase handler. Verify exact pinned implementation; do not fake an enchantment by selling only the base item.
- Current quest rewards use `hqs coins add {p} N` as a compatibility bridge around the pinned Quest Shop `void` reward ABI; Bountiful native command-reward support is a promising integration point, **not yet proven for exact per-player/team payout and single claim**.
- Currency belongs to shared FTB Teams' Quest Shop account; identify the actual redeemed player (not global selectors); avoid duplicate credits from multiple teammates/redeems. Keep separate MXP/Path progression unaffected.
- Avoid broad anti-exploit overengineering: run focused checks for duplicate claims, coin minting loops, returns/resales, invalid components, and bypass of actual boss/progression gates. Intentional renewable money and repeatable bounty income are allowed.

### Required work-slice inventory (per AGENTS.md)

**Implementation/code-ready after owner direction, pending workstream ownership / exact-schema verification:**
- [ ] Extend Bountiful reward compiler/config to express the three decree family payout policies while preserving currently owner-approved thematic reward pools and gate protections. Coordinate #365's active writer.
- [ ] Replace `tmm_hunting` arrows/leather reward pool with coin-only *after* verifying native command reward codec, correct claim-time player context, and team currency credit; add static regression assertions.
- [ ] Expand canonical `manifest/quest_shop_catalog.json`, generated KubeJS shop datapack entries/categories and validators for ordinary stack items, rare ingredients, foods and individual Relics/Artifacts; do registry+component census first.
- [ ] Design and implement component-aware shop purchases for custom enchantments/equipment if pinned Quest Shop cannot express them; isolate addon/bridge to avoid fork if possible.

**Explicit owner-level design decisions remaining:**
- [ ] Payout distributions for mixed general and rare specialist coin rewards; relative payouts/effort for hunting and Gateways.
- [ ] Detailed shop stock eligibility and gated-item exceptions, individual prices and available enchantment tiers.
- [ ] Whether custom enchanted stock/Relics use fixed components or randomized quality; resolve exact semantics before implementation.

**In-game gameplay acceptance queue (after reviewed integration and separately authorized build):**
- [ ] **Type C:** Complete ordinary general contracts and verify both coin and item results over enough rolls, without every claim requiring both.
- [ ] **Type C:** Complete several `tmm_hunting` contracts as non-Hunter/Hunter; each credits only Quest Shop team coins exactly once and no arrows/leather. Check repeated slips, two teammates, relog, multiple boards and overflow.
- [ ] **Type C:** Complete magic-school contracts (especially Iron's) and verify material results dominate, rare coin outcomes occur at approved rate, and protected rewards/gates remain intact.
- [ ] **Type C:** Buy supplies, prepared foods and diet-appropriate provisions; buy real enchanted books/gear and fresh Relics/Artifacts, confirm exact components/enchants, coin debit and persistence after relog.
- [ ] **Type C:** Start a fresh test-world mercenary-only career; earn enough to purchase food, equipment, upgrades and a high-priced Relic **without required farming/mining/loot RNG**. Record earnings/time and adjust balance.
- [ ] **Type A + C:** Targeted duplicate-claim, team-account, recipe/EMC/shop resale and gate-bypass regression checks. Do not turn this into a universal ban on profitable farms.

### Ownership / coordination

Quest Shop catalog + validator edit ownership: designated modpack integration writer via isolated PR. Bountiful rewards/coin binding: #365 and its designated author. Preserve all existing source/branch and QA authorization boundaries. **This issue records a design target only; it does not itself authorize a full build or gameplay modification.**

Related: #365 (Bountiful), #47 (EMC mapping), #44 (ProjectE), [current shop catalog](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/blob/test/full-integration/manifest/quest_shop_catalog.json), [shop architecture](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/blob/test/full-integration/docs/QUEST-SHOP-ECONOMY.md).

## Approved shop navigation requirement — 2026-11-22

**Goal:** The player must be able to open a specific shop section immediately, **without scrolling past all preceding sections/items**. The growing catalog needs actual *category filtering/navigation*, not merely visual grouping.

**Current technical observation:** Quest Shop 1.4.0's upstream `ShopMenuScreen.refreshEntries()` groups purchases by category, sorts them, then flattens every category header and every item into **one continuous `ShopList`**. The header rows in `CategoryHeaderEntry` are nonselectable; the stock UI offers **no category tabs/filter selector**. New `shop_categories/*.json` files alone will not achieve the requested navigation. Reference: https://github.com/alexanderheuts/quest-shop/blob/main/src/main/java/com/holysweet/questshop/client/screen/ShopMenuScreen.java .

**Preferred UI design:**
- A visible **category selector** (sidebar, tabs, or a compact dropdown appropriate to screen size); clicking a section filters the item list to **only that section**.
- Independent scrolling *within* the selected section; selecting another category must be fast without returning to top of the full catalog.
- Preserve the player's visible coin balance and accessible Buy button, disabled state/affordability, category lock indication, vanilla keyboard/controller usability where supported, and server-validated purchases.
- A **search field** across the active section (ideally optional "all items" global search) is desirable as the catalog expands, but category filtering is the primary acceptance requirement.
- Provisional shop taxonomy (adapt exact names/counts to registry and legibility): **Supplies & Building; Ores & Minerals; Food & Potions; Magical Reagents; Weapons & Armor; Enchantments; Repairs & Utilities; Exploration Finds; Relics & Artifacts**. Distinct magic schools can be subcategories later if necessary. Do not require a separate purchasable category for each mod initially.
- Every item must have exactly one understandable home category in the catalog; avoid duplicating entries to work around navigation.

**Engineering work / readiness:**
- [ ] **Implementation-ready concept, exact pinned ABI and UI strategy to verify:** inspect Quest Shop 1.4.0 JAR and current integrated GUI APIs; choose small, isolated client UI extension/patch (or alternative compatible approach), rather than assuming datapack-only categories solve navigation. Respect original mod license and minimize divergence from upstream.
- [ ] **Implementation-ready data** after taxonomy selection: split/rename the category metadata and canonical catalog/entries consistently; adjust `scripts/validate_quests.py` so its current six-category constraint is not a hard blocker to approved expansion.
- [ ] **Implementation-ready checks:** automated verification that all categories are reachable, every product assigned to valid category, and client filtering never sends wrong product/category IDs in the buy payload.
- [ ] **Type C gameplay test** after separately authorized integrated build: switch directly from Food to Relics to Ores without scrolling through intervening items, inspect long category list, buy an item in two sections, test lock state, insufficient funds, coin decrement, and return to the shop after relog.
- [ ] **Design choice still open:** final sidebar/tab/dropdown visual arrangement at Minecraft screen sizes, exact names and whether search spans all categories. The specific illustrative layout is not fixed.

**Scope:** This is part of #523's expanded shop and supports the existing bounty-funded adventurer playstyle. **No immediate runtime change or full build/QA authorization** follows from design recording.

## Read-only replacement survey — 2026-11-22 (NOT an inclusion decision)

Owner asked whether repeated problems with current Quest Shop justify evaluating replacement.

**Leading capability-fit candidate: Q Shop 1.8.5** (NeoForge 1.21.1, CurseForge https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/q-shop/files/9407426). Its native sub-shop tabs, searchable current tab, extensive editable catalogue, item NBT/Base64 stacks, custom currencies, command entries and KubeJS/FTB integrations address most missing UI/catalog behaviors without changing its renderer. It also permits shop templates in `config/qshop/`. Source 1.21.1 branch: https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/tree/neoforge-1.21.1 .

**Two important unresolved blockers:**
1. **Per-player wallet:** official docs and NeoForge WalletCapability store balances per player, not per FTB team. Existing Quest Shop is FTB Teams-shared; migration or a team-wallet bridge changes semantics. Do not invent a naive on-join synchronization (duplicates/races). Owner decision required whether currency should remain team-shared, become personal, or justify tested compat.
2. **FTB reward API discrepancy:** inspected `src/main/java/com/qshop/ftb/QShopMoneyReward.java` on `neoforge-1.21.1` declares `public void claim(ServerPlayer, boolean)`, while FTB Quests 1.21.1/main `Reward.java` declares `public abstract boolean claim(...)`. This resembles the already observed Quest Shop 1.4.0 reward ABI failure. Verify exact official **1.8.5** JAR; do not use native `qshop:money` reward until proven. Authorized FTB Quests command reward invoking `/qshop currency give ...` may avoid this specific ABI, but must be tested for once-only payment/permissions.

**Alternate: Team Economy 1.0.2** (NeoForge 1.21.1, https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/team-economy), native FTB Teams shared wallet, categories and search, vanilla enchanted books, configurable modded item catalog, claim-id-based `/teamecon reward` and `/teamecon_quest_reward` commands. However it bundles six game machines, scratch tickets, mystery boxes and five wallet equipment levels, which may add unwanted systems; supports no third-party enchantment stock according to published docs. Evaluate disabling/isolating these and component-bearing ItemStacks before selection.

**Other screened:** Merchantry (NeoForge 1.21.1 server-side shop and repair; personal currency + many unrelated mechanics), LingGemShop (sidebar/search and FTB Quests integration but unrelated Create-heavy defaults and unclear team semantics), Pomelo's Shop (nested categories, personal balances, lower release maturity), World Shop (team wallet/FTB native but current CurseForge lists only NeoForge 26.1.2, incompatible with MC 1.21.1). Sources: provider CurseForge/Modrinth pages.

**Next action:** no pin/replacement now. Perform bounded source/JAR compatibility audit of QShop + Team Economy; test exact FTB 2101.1.38, Bountiful payouts, vanilla/modded enchanted gear, rare relic initialization, quick navigation, persistence, multiplayer claiming, and catalog migration. Respect explicit full-build/QA authorization gate. If personal vs shared wallet is settled, choose pilot candidate and isolate catalog conversion/rollback. Current #523 design and all 48 offers remain intact pending decision.

comments.text: **Owner decision finalized 2026-11-22:** Q Shop 1.8.5 replaces Quest Shop; **coins are per-player, NOT team-shared**. Migration implementation is in [PR #531](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/531), 48/48 existing offer parity in six native tabs, old mod/config removed, twelve FTB resource-sale rewards now target personal wallet through `qshop currency give {p} coins 1`. This is source work pending integration review/quick CI; **no full build dispatched**. Current old team balances are not migrated automatically; next QA should use a fresh disposable world. Expanded ink/enchanted gear/Relics catalog still follows as separate #523 work.

comments.text:
## Owner-proposed follow-on feature: rotating `SALE!` offers — 2026-11-22

**Requested gameplay concept:** Add a prominent, independently navigable **SALE!** shop tab with a rotating roster of rare, desirable goods at meaningful discounts. This is intended as a fun reason to return between Bountiful contracts and a bounty-money sink, *not* a new required progression gate or a replacement for normal static offers.

**Technical feasibility (verified against Q Shop 1.21.1 upstream):** Q Shop has native KubeJS `QShop.refreshTab(shopRef, tabUuid, count, weightedPool)`; supports item stacks, prices, descriptions, player limits and custom currency. It saves the resulting shop and broadcasts updates to clients. **Caveat:** the native sampler picks WITH replacement (duplicates possible within a refresh) and regenerates entry UUIDs/purchase limits. Rotation timing is NOT supplied by the API. Implement a small KubeJS server-side scheduler/controlled unique selection and persistent rotation marker (across reloads and restarts); do not refresh on each tick or reset one-per-person limits merely by logging back in. Ensure opening a shop during a refresh remains server-authoritative.

**Suggested initial design for playtest, not locked prices/cadence:**
- One `SALE!` tab shown at the top of `/qshop open tmm`, with **4 distinct offers per rotation**. Common sale candidates: high-tier Iron's inks, rare magical reagents, specific enchantment books/gear, and collectible Artifacts/Relics (once #523 expansion items are authored/registry-verified).
- **~25–45% off a canonical regular shop list price**; very rare stronger discounts, not free or below zero. Show normal price and discounted price clearly in custom offer names/descriptions. Do not arbitrarily invent new normal prices for items not yet in the catalog: sale candidates need validated base prices first.
- **One purchase per player, per offer, per rotation** as default; same selection across the server, personal wallets. Avoid global first-come-first-served stock, since late joiners should get a chance.
- **Adjustable rotation cadence**; proposed initial playtest default = every **3 Minecraft days**, with an unambiguous visible next-refresh marker. This is a proposal; schedule/slots/discount bands are configurable and owner may tune after testing.
- No boss-only, transformation initiation, ritual-gated or blacklisted items. The ordinary shop remains available at normal prices when sale ends. No quests or paywalls for seeing SALE!.
- Prefer weighted rare/very rare entry pools for novelty, but no duplicates in the same roster. A generic recurring price reduction on cobblestone is not the objective.

**Work-slice ledger:** 
- [ ] **Design/tuning**: confirm default cadence, count, eligibility, per-player limits, rarity weight, discount band, visible refresh information. Owner-proposed concept; sample values not final approvals.
- [ ] **Code-ready after those values are settled:** create stable `SALE!` tab in Q Shop template, add data-driven candidate pool to canonical shop source, implement persistently scheduled KubeJS roll with no duplicate offers and no reset on every load; keep original base catalog immutable.
- [ ] **Type A** static tests for at most one occurrence/item, positive discounted amounts, all targets in approved purchaseable registry, timer state preserved, and category/Packwiz consistency.
- [ ] **Type C** next separately authorized Minecraft gameplay QA: discounts match labels, rotation updates on intended cadence, persistent state/claim limits across restart and relog, personal-only purchase eligibility, tab updates while open, normal stock unaffected, and multiplayer late-joiner behavior.

**Scope coordination:** This follows the actual migration PR #531, which is currently reviewable and should stay focused on porting the 48 old offers. The SALE! addition is a **separate follow-on PR/feature**, not a reason to delay that migration. It does not authorize full server/client QA or a new Minecraft build.

Source: https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/blob/neoforge-1.21.1/KUBEJS_WIKI.md#random-tab-refresh ; implementation: https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/blob/neoforge-1.21.1/src/main/java/com/qshop/kubejs/QShopBindings.java (refreshTab).

## Candidate implementation for equipment inventory — use Apotheosis native generated gear (owner suggestion 2026-11-22)

**Question:** Instead of manually designing and serializing a huge set of enchanted armor/weapons, use the randomly rolled equipment Apotheosis itself offers via the Wandering Trader.

**Verified feasibility in pinned source:** TMM pins **Apotheosis 1.21.1-8.9.0**. Its `src/main/java/dev/shadowsoffire/apotheosis/affix/trades/AutomaticAffixTrade.java` generates affix equipment using `GenContext.forPlayer(...)` (player world tier, luck, dimension/biome) and `LootController.createRandomLootItem`; adds `Components.FROM_TRADER`. Datagen provides ten `apotheosis:automatic_affix_trade` entries (`wanderer_trades/affix/automatic_1..10`). Named preset trade definitions `wanderer_trades/rare_gear/*.json` include heavily enchanted items (Bonesplitter, Stonebreaker, Greatplate of Eternity, etc.) in SUMMIT/PINNACLE tiers. Changelog 8.3.2 says Wandering Traders sell affixed items again; 8.9.0 source matches our pin. This is different from random vanilla enchants.

**Recommended shape (concept, pending exact purchase presentation decision):**
- Let Apotheosis own rarity distributions, affixes, and equipment compatibility. Do not create a competing homebrew enchanted item matrix.
- Equip the regular **Weapons & Armor** Q Shop tab with thematic random equipment offers (optional weapon vs armor split) that produce a real Apotheosis affix-bearing stack, retaining exactly the native component data. Use base prices reflecting rarity and avoid boss-gated raw materials and inappropriate world-tier jumps.
- For the rotating **SALE!** tab prefer **pre-rolled, visible exact gear** (like the Wandering Trader's offer) so the customer can inspect the modifiers before paying. This is friendlier than an undisclosed paid random lootbox. Use Q Shop's true component-bearing ItemStack purchase entries if a safe KubeJS/native bridge can pre-roll and persist a stack.
- If pre-roll is not straightforward, an alternate technically viable route is a Q Shop `COMMAND` purchase via a **custom loot table** using Apotheosis's `apotheosis:random_affix_item` loot pool entry or `apotheosis:reforge_item` loot function; this produces random gear **at redemption**, thus the shop preview can't display exact affixes. It must be visibly labeled RANDOM/UNKNOWN and properly verified under the `/loot` player context (Apotheosis's `GenContext.forLoot` requires a player in loot parameters). Do not silently confuse it with the trader's pre-rolled item.
- Named `rare_gear` offers can be ported from official trade output **ItemStack components** and sold as curated high-end specials, subject to the SAME Summit/Pinnacle rules rather than cheaply bypassing world-tier progression.
- Q Shop `refreshTab` randomizes an offer **list of preconfigured item stacks**, not Apotheosis affixes. It is insufficient on its own: a generation/redemption bridge, and safe wallet debit+grant sequencing, is still required.

**Work-slices / test queue:**
- [ ] Engineering: prototype one affix sword and one armor offer through both methods; verify 8.9.0 generator APIs, retained affix/rareness data, restricted loot categories, and Q Shop's display/item persistence semantics.
- [ ] Design: decide whether standard shop offers reveal the exact roll or deliberately buy a random grade; SALE! should favor revealed pre-rolled stock.
- [ ] Type A: data-component payload and permission/context checks; strict rarity/price ceiling and no hidden gate bypass.
- [ ] Type C next authorized gameplay: client view matches purchased stack; tier-based generation and modded enchantments; login/restart persistence, personal coin debit exactly once, no empty purchase; two-player independent wallets.
- [ ] Keep #531 migration pure; implement in separate #523 shop catalog expansion once basic Q Shop is in the tested integrated branch.

Sources: https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apotheosis/blob/1.21/src/main/java/dev/shadowsoffire/apotheosis/affix/trades/AutomaticAffixTrade.java , https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apotheosis/blob/1.21/src/main/java/dev/shadowsoffire/apotheosis/loot/LootController.java , https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apotheosis/blob/1.21/src/generated/resources/data/apotheosis/loot_table/chests/tome_tower.json , https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/blob/neoforge-1.21.1/KUBEJS_WIKI.md .

comments.text:
## Owner equipment-shop refinement — 2026-11-22: enchantment-based, seven diamond-equivalent slots

**Approved design direction from owner (SUPERSEDES the previous suggestion to center randomized affix equipment):**

1. **Permanent standard stock:** Always-available, individually identified weapons, armor, and everyday tools **through iron tier** (include base wood/stone/leather/chain/gold/iron equivalents as appropriate to their actual stats/recipes). Ordinary base items, no random rolls; predictable per-item pricing in personal Q Shop `coins`. Modded low-tier equivalents require validated registries and explicit balance review.
2. **Exactly seven premium equipment slots, always populated**: `sword`, `axe`, `pickaxe`, `helmet`, `chestplate`, `leggings`, `boots`. Each slot generates **one diamond-tier / diamond-equivalent eligible piece**, with **random choice of the base item within that equipment category** and **random high-level enchantments** modeled on Apotheosis/Apothic Enchanting's extraordinary Wandering Trader named gear. The category of each slot is fixed, *not* another random roll. No explicit requirement to use affix loot; **enchantments, not affixes**, are the target.
3. **Pre-roll and persist** each offer server-side for a shop stock cycle, including the *whole* ItemStack (enchantments, custom name, any supported components). All players see the same seven offers and their **actual enchantments and exact coin price before paying**. No reroll on click, per-shop open, login, or every server boot. We can align to the planned SALE! rotation after cadence is finalized; no schedule has been approved for the equipment stock specifically.
4. **Rarity and legality:** Enchant compatibility (valid item tags/slots, exclusivity, no curses unless explicitly decided), in-scope rarity and weighted level bands, and no boss/ritual/transformation bypass. Enchantment upper bounds come from **Apothic Enchanting's live 1.21.1 config/EnchantmentInfo** and supported high-tier item entries, not an arbitrary assumption that vanilla `Enchantment.getMaxLevel` is enough. Existing named Wandering Trader `rare_gear/*.json` provides evidence of heavily enchanted items beyond ordinary vanilla levels, but its named fixed presets are *not themselves random enchantment generators*.
5. **Pricing:** seven premium slots priced substantially above comparable plain-iron goods, varied by equipment class and enchantment quality; no exact coin prices invented yet. A rolled premium piece can also enter the separate SALE! roster at a genuine discount, if no purchase/stock/reroll exploit. Keep the regular shop an alternative livelihood, not an arbitrary bonus loot vending machine.
6. **Potential item source pool:** vanilla diamond equipment + separately verified diamond-equivalent modded weapons/armor/tools per category. An item category with only one eligible base type will naturally randomize *enchantments* but not item identity until more approved equivalents are available. Do not silently include netherite, boss weapons, enchanted accessories or gated transform forms as substitutes.

**Verified implementation interfaces (not yet integrated):**
- Q Shop 1.8.5 `EntryBuilder.buy(Object item)` accepts `net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack`; Q Shop JSON uses a base64 compressed serialized ItemStack for full components, saved in the world shop file. `QShop.entry('tmm', tabUuid).buy(actualStack).price(coins, 'coins').uuid(stableSlotId).add()` can replace the offer for each fixed slot. Confirm exact KubeJS-to-Java wrapper in 1.21.1 runtime, since objects may need conversion.
- Q Shop `refreshTab` only randomly selects **preconfigured entries**; it does **not** generate random enchantments. Pre-rolling correctly requires a small KubeJS/native API adapter or first-party code that constructs safe, enchanted ItemStacks using the server enchantment registry, then hands the result to Q Shop. No purchase-time OP command/undisclosed random roll should be used by default.
- `ApothicEnchanting.ENCHANTMENT_INFO` and `EnchantmentInfo.getMaxLevel/getMaxLootLevel` are separately configurable; former is intended general cap and latter for loot/villager sources. Which limits the shop emulates must be matched to verified trader behavior and config; never roll invalid combinations or levels outside the chosen effective cap. Apotheosis 8.9.0's `rare_gear/*.json` shows named exceptionally enchanted gear, while `AutomaticAffixTrade` generates **affixed** items and is **not** the chosen mechanism.
- The upstream Q Shop 1.21.1 source stores full item components via `ShopJson.stackToBase64/stackFromBase64`. Validate all modded enchantment registry data survives serialization and displays properly; do not rely on a vanilla `nbt` object, which Q Shop treats only as custom data.

**Slices (design vs implementation vs QA):**
- [x] **Design settled:** permanent equipment through iron; 7 fixed categories for premium stock; random eligible diamond-equivalent item and compatible strong enchantments; pre-rolled visible stock; personal wallet; affix-only generation is NOT the intended feature.
- [ ] **Implementation-ready static slice:** expand Q Shop catalog/config + Packwiz/index/validator with ordinary equipment up to iron tier, preserving the original 48 entries, no prior shop migration rewrite. Author in separate feature PR after #531 rather than muddying the base migration.
- [ ] **Implementation-ready adapter research/prototype:** identify usable 1.21.1 item/enchantment registry APIs, valid enchanting power/maximum levels, compatibility groups, component serialization and Q Shop `EntryBuilder` ItemStack support.
- [ ] **Further design tuning:** approved eligible modded diamond-equivalent item lists, price bands, whether premium stock refresh follows SALE! cadence, and per-player purchase limit per roll. These decisions do not block static iron-tier work or adapter tests.
- [ ] **Type A:** static valid category counts; permanent entries and exactly seven rotating slots; bounded selection, item registration, enchant max and compatibility, no duplicates/bypass, indexed files and deterministic roll persistence marker.
- [ ] **Type C after owner-authorized build:** actual enchanted components/UI/purchase parity and persistence, 7 fixed categories through refresh, personal coins once, dedicated server/2 players/reload, and original plain gear always available.

Sources: https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apotheosis/blob/1.21/src/main/java/dev/shadowsoffire/apotheosis/data/WandererTradesProvider.java ; https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apothic-Enchanting/blob/1.21/src/main/java/dev/shadowsoffire/apothic_enchanting/EnchantmentInfo.java ; https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/blob/neoforge-1.21.1/src/main/java/com/qshop/shop/ShopJson.java ; https://github.com/QLNPLUS/Q-shop/blob/neoforge-1.21.1/src/main/java/com/qshop/kubejs/EntryBuilder.java .

**Branch/authorization:** #531 remains isolated original migration PR, unmerged and source-verified; no full build/Prism/ingame QA authorized here.

## CURRENT equipment shop decision — 2026-11-22 (supersedes broad "through iron" and affix-focused proposals)

**Owner choice:** Use TWO clearly separated Q Shop sections, `Iron Gear` and `Enchanted Diamond`; do **not** stock the wood/stone/leather progression tiers. This comment supersedes earlier suggestions to sell all early gear tiers or use randomly affixed Apotheosis equipment.

**Iron Gear — always available:** base iron sword, iron axe, iron pickaxe, iron helmet, iron chestplate, iron leggings and iron boots as deterministic affordable personal-coin purchases. Any shovel/hoe additions are a separate sensible inventory extension, not essential to the seven combat/mining slots. No enchantment randomness on the iron products. This is a pure data/config extension, separate PR from baseline migration #531.

**Enchanted Diamond — seven premium categories:** one rolled diamond/dimension-equivalent equipment **offer** in each of sword, axe, pickaxe, helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots. Keep each category always represented. Randomize both eligible actual base item (only where alternate diamond-equivalent items have been explicitly validated) and the *compatible high-power enchantments and their levels*; do not use Apotheosis **affixes** as a substitute. Roll one exact server-authoritative ItemStack per slot **on shop-stock refresh**; preview the full genuine stack, its enchantments, and personal-coin price BEFORE purchase. Persist across save/reload; no purchase-time lottery, no reroll on shop open/login. Rotation cadence and budget/prices to be tuned separately; ordinary permanent iron stock does not rotate. For now, seven vanilla diamond equipment types are the safe baseline—other equivalent modded items require a registry/eligibility pass.

### Codex installed-binary audit changes the implementation strategy

[PR #544](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/544), source report [README](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/blob/audit/apotheosis-trader-gear-2026-11-22/docs/qa/APOTHEOSIS-TRADER-GEAR-2026-11-22/README.md), analyzed exactly the installed Apotheosis **8.9.0** resources and save (24 entity-region files / 660 populated chunks). Found only **ten named enchanted-diamond presets** (3 swords, 2 axes, 1 pickaxe, 4 armor pieces) and **no arbitrary random enchanted-item generator** from this trader source. All ten named outputs are fixed combos offered only in **Summit/Pinnacle** tiers. One observed saved Wandering Trader had no diamond offers; snapshot absence **does not** prove trades are broken. TMM's custom trader injection instead uses a different **random affix** item path. This audit is excellent *template/cap/slot* evidence but **not an implementation shortcut** for the requested random enchantments.

**Correct technical path:**
- Read a selected level-appropriate enchantment pool from live server enchantment registry and Apothic Enchanting 1.6.4's effective enchantment/loot caps, configured exclusivity/compatibility and modded supports; use native `minecraft:enchantments` on ItemStacks, not raw custom NBT or hidden trader-affix rolls.
- Either author a small first-party server-side random enchanting service or a tested KubeJS/native bridge; apply per-slot enchant selection and level band rules. The ten installed pre-enchanted trader presets are concrete fixtures for realistic power combinations, not a ten-entry picklist substitute.
- Q Shop's 1.21.1 Builder `QShop.entry('tmm', tabUuid).buy(actualItemStack).price(...).uuid(stableSlotId).add()` accepts Java ItemStacks; `ShopJson` stores full compressed ItemStack data, but its registry access is constructed from `BuiltInRegistries.REGISTRY`. **Investigate whether dynamic 1.21 enchantment registry references survive Q Shop disk round-trip**; source promise alone is not gameplay proof. If not, design a narrow server-registry-aware bridge instead of silently selling unenchanted diamond items or modifying third-party binary.
- Existing `QShop.refreshTab` only picks pre-existing entries (and samples with replacement). It **cannot invent enchantment layouts**. Use stable slot identities and a persisted roll snapshot/refresh generation ID, and don't clear player limits unintentionally.
- Preserve boss/ritual/transformation-gated gear exclusions; avoid unapproved Netherite, endgame-only or overlevelled bypasses. Gear from the trader's Summit/Pinnacle samples suggests power-level gating needs an explicit shop policy/price calibration, NOT automatic free availability at world start.

**Implementation-ready slices:**
- [ ] Permanent seven ordinary iron entries, `Iron Gear` Q Shop section, catalog, index and validator update in a new expansion PR following #531.
- [ ] `Enchanted Diamond` section with seven stable slot placeholders and validation of one per category, no empty/unenchanted dummy BUY stock.
- [ ] First-party/KubeJS prototype for high-power compatible enchanted diamond ItemStacks, full Q Shop component round-trip/restart and server-authoritative persistence; test two disjoint classes (sword + chestplate).
- [ ] Add randomized generator for all seven, matching a bounded enchant weight/level specification with uniqueness of slots and change-only-on-explicit rotation.

**Design tuning remaining (not code blocker for iron stock):** exact level/number-of-enchants distribution, minimum world/quest gate vs high coin pricing, refresh cadence (could share SALE! cycle), purchase limit per player per offer, and approved eligible modded diamond-equivalents. Do not invent fixed prices.

**QA:** Type A check 7 iron stock, 7 premium slots, no pre-diamond stock, enchantment compatibility/caps, deterministic roll/persistence; Type C next authorized world: exactly matching preview/granted stack, one player debit/claim, two-player checkout, reload survival, category changes at proper cadence, no server crashes, no hard-gate bypass. No full build authorized by this design decision.

**Issue governance:** #523 original body includes legacy *Quest Shop team wallet* and old client GUI assumptions; those are superseded by owner-approved personal wallet Q Shop migration #531. This comment is authoritative for equipment scope; do not reintroduce retired team coins or primitive shop JSON paths.

## HAND-AUTHORED ENCHANTED DIAMOND ROSTER — OWNER DESIGN PIVOT (2026-11-22)

**Supersedes the previous generator approach.** The shop should not generate arbitrary affix or enchantment combinations. Author **four distinct named, fixed enchantment sets for each of seven diamond equipment slots = 28 genuine ItemStack presets**, each with an individual thematic focus and at least one signature enchantment *unique among that same slot's four variants*. The **seven available premium Q Shop offers** are randomized by selecting **one of four authored choices per slot** whenever the roster rotates. All seven slots remain represented; the *contents* of each preset are deterministic. **Permanent equipment stock is IRON ONLY:** one regular Q Shop `Iron Gear` section with the iron sword, iron axe, iron pickaxe and four iron armor pieces. NO wood, stone, leather, chain or gold gear as basic stock. Separate `Enchanted Diamond` tab holds the seven rotating curated diamond offers.

**Enchantment strength policy:** No vanilla enchant exceeds its vanilla maximum by **more than one**, and one-level effects (Mending, Silk Touch, Aqua Affinity) stay at I rather than artificially II. Apotheosis/Apothic Enchanting enchantments stay at or below their own 1.21 source maxima and server configured/hard cap. Not every enchant must be at the upper limit; specs below are a balanced *draft*, not final price approval. Each has 3–4 enchants. No unapproved curses, generic AffixLootController rolls, exclusive pair combinations, or magic-gate bypass.

**Concrete design draft — all 28 named items:**

**Verified modded IDs (Apothic Enchanting 1.21):** `knowledge_of_the_ages` (sword/sharp weapon; turns drops into XP), `scavenger` (sharp weapon, bonus loot), `chainsaw` (axe only), `boon_of_the_earth` (pickaxe only), `miners_fervor` (mining; mutually exclusive with Efficiency), `icy_thorns` (chestplate; mutually exclusive with vanilla Thorns), `rebounding` (chest/legs), `berserkers_fury` (chestplate only), `stable_footing` (boots). Multi-protection types, Fortune/Silk Touch, Efficiency/Miner's Fervor, Mending/Life Mending, Thorns/Icy Thorns, Frost Walker/Depth Strider must remain separate. `Chainsaw`, `Scavenger` and `Rebounding` are confirmed by upstream for the specified equipment families. **Slice tracking:**

- [ ] Code-ready content slice: create declarative JSON preset roster with 28 entries plus seven iron entries; keep Q Shop migration #531 unmodified. Exact existing registry/compatible enchant validation is Type A gate.
- [ ] Code-ready runtime slice: lightweight KubeJS preset selection/persistence and Q Shop seven-slot update plus full component-bearing item data, without custom enchant generator. Fixed UUIDs, configurable refresh interval and pricing.
- [ ] Design tuning: confirm final name/level combos if desired; prices/stock cadence, sale discounts and per-player purchase caps remain to be balanced. None block isolated content authoring and initial registry tests.
- [ ] Type A: validate all 28 sets, slot/signature uniqueness, 3–4 enchant counts, live registries, tiers/exclusions, nonzero prices, index integrity, and reproducible selected seven.
- [ ] Type C after authorized full-build: verify display/granted item identity and enchants, permanence of iron, seven slots at once, single successful debit, persistent rotation and personal limits, multiplayer and cross-restart stock.
- [ ] Integration ownership: new expansion PR after #531 Q Shop migration, no edits to Bountiful's separately owned #365 payouts, no full QA or Minecraft build authorized here.

**Source evidence:** installed 8.9.0 trader audit [PR #544](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/544) confirms only ten named pre-enchanted items with much higher fixed enchant levels (Summit/Pinnacle), and separately affixed random offers. [Apothic Enchanting's supported item definitions](https://github.com/Shadows-of-Fire/Apothic-Enchanting/tree/1.21/src/generated/resources/data/apothic_enchanting/enchantment) verify custom enchantment slot compatibility. The authored presets intentionally need neither of those trader generation systems.

**Supersedes previous 28-preset draft in this issue.** Owner wants much **less ordinary Mending**, broader representation of existing mods' surprising enchantments, including benefits *with genuine costs*, and **no more than one entirely vanilla-enchanted item per equipment category**. This revision retains the previously discussed seven premium diamond gear slots, four authored alternatives per slot = 28 named presets. The basic `Iron Gear` shop stock remains just seven regular iron pieces. No arbitrary enchantment generator.

The table uses short mod prefixes to avoid ambiguity; actual registry IDs are:
- **Apothic Enchanting 1.6.4** `apothic_enchanting:knowledge_of_the_ages`, `scavenger`, `chainsaw`, `life_mending`, `miners_fervor`, `boon_of_the_earth`, `berserkers_fury`, `icy_thorns`, `rebounding`, `stable_footing`.

- **EvilCraft 1.2.102** `evilcraft:life_stealing`, `breaking`, `vengeance`, `unusing`.

### What players learn from each
- **Knowledge of the Ages**: mob drops become XP (works naturally with the uncommon Mending piece).
- **Life Mending**: consumes health to repair the item, **mutually exclusive with standard Mending**; a deliberately risky durability tool.
- **Berserker's Fury**: a health-priced combat buff, on chestplates.
- **Miner's Fervor**: alternative capped/sustained mining speed, **mutually exclusive with Efficiency**.
- **Boon of the Earth**: bonus mining finds (pickaxe-only).
- **Chainsaw**: tree cutting on axes.
- **Icy Thorns**: alternative cold retaliation effect, **mutually exclusive with vanilla Thorns**.
- **Rebounding**: retaliation on armor, supports chestplate and leggings.
- **Stable Footing**: specialty movement effect on boots.
- **Ars mana boost/regen**: magic gear on ordinary diamond armor, useful even when the equipment isn't specialized Ars armor.
- **Ars Reactive**: enchantment is legal on these vanilla items, but reactive spell activation generally requires the item/spell to be configured in Ars. Ensure sold gear is actually functional out-of-box, or annotate as customizable to avoid inert stock.
- **EvilCraft Life Stealing**: heals from weapon damage; **Breaking** increases held-item wear, **Unusing** prevents attempted attacks/mining when item is near breaking, **Vengeance** can summon vengeance spirits when hitting/breaking. **Source verification:** Apothic Enchanting 1.21 branch is `version=1.6.4, mcVersion=1.21.1`; Ars main branch `mod_version=5.13.5, minecraft_version=1.21.1`; EvilCraft **master-1.21-lts** `mod_version=1.2.102, minecraft_version=1.21.1`. Their native enchantment resource JSON supports correct equipment classes and max modded levels. IMPORTANT: EvilCraft `master-1.21` is for Minecraft 1.21.11 and must not be used as TMM's authority; the LTS branch was subsequently inspected. All modded max levels in the draft match their own JSON max levels; vanilla max+1 cap per owner.

**Revision validation:** 7 categories × 4 = 28; **exactly 7 vanilla-only** options (one per class); only **2 standard Mending I** pieces, **4 Life Mending** pieces; other 22 do not have either. All preset counts 3–4 enchantments. Explicitly avoid known pairs: Miner's Fervor + Efficiency, Life Mending + Mending, Icy Thorns + Thorns, Frost Walker + Depth Strider, Fortune + Silk Touch. Every item has a distinct focus and at least one distinguishing enchantment relative to the other three *within its category*.

**Implementation plan after owner response:** This is purely authored data: one server-defined item stack per preset with exact named display/enchant components; when rotating Q Shop's `Enchanted Diamond` stock choose one of four from each equipment category and persist seven selected entries, all seven equipment types present. No enchantment-generation API required. `Iron Gear` remains permanent. Source validation still needed for modded enchant supported item tags, in-game data-component serialization, configured vanilla max+1 handling, and Ars Reactive usability. Use separate expansion PR, not migration PR #531; shop costs and rotation cadence not yet approved.

**Ownership and test queue:** type A: namespace registry check, compatibility/power-level caps, all 28 presets and seven selected slots, templates vs emitted items, module preservation/Packwiz index. Type C after approved build: actual enchantments + behavior and their downsides, Q Shop preview vs purchase/coin debit, per-player wallets, stock refresh/restart, Reactive spell functionality. No full Minecraft build/QA authorized here.

## Owner correction — REMOVE Reactive from every authored diamond shop item (2026-11-22)

**Binding design change:** Reactive `ars_nouveau:reactive` is **not allowed on any pre-authored TMM enchanted diamond purchase**. Unlike normal magical effects, Reactive is useless without a specifically configured spell component. The native Ars Nouveau `ReactiveEnchantmentRecipe#assemble` attaches `ars_nouveau` Reactive Caster data from a spell parchment, and the proposed shop's plain enchantment component doesn't do that. Do not substitute an unconfigured Reactive item in any sale. Preserve 7 classes × 4 alternatives and exactly one vanilla-only alternative per class.

Replace these four entries in the latest 28-preset draft:

| Class | Superseded | Replacement | Full authored enchantments | Signature / focus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Helmet | Reactive Circlet (Reactive III) | **Borrowed Clarity** | `apothic_enchanting:life_mending II`, `ars_nouveau:mana_boost II`, Projectile Protection V, Unbreaking IV | Life Mending trades health for repair; mana equipment |
| Chestplate | Arcane Deflection (Reactive IV) | **Vengeful Bulwark** | `apothic_enchanting:rebounding III`, `ars_nouveau:mana_boost III`, Protection V, Unbreaking IV | Rebounding retaliates; mana |
| Leggings | Spellwoven Trousers (Reactive III) | **Pain Dividend** | `apothic_enchanting:life_mending II`, `ars_nouveau:mana_boost III`, Projectile Protection V, Thorns III | Health-price self-repair + mana |
| Boots | Icebreaker (Reactive III) | **Icebreaker** (revised) | `ars_nouveau:mana_boost III`, Frost Walker III, Fire Protection V, Unbreaking III | Mana + walking on water/ice |

All other latest-draft options unchanged. This is a **design handoff, not runtime source implementation**. The seven vanilla-only options remain unchanged. Replacements intentionally stay within native eligible item tags and known modded level caps; compile-time validations and Type C real gameplay checks still required.

Related **independent loot hygiene**: see [#328](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/issues/328) for excluding *unconfigured* Reactive enchanted books from loot rolls without disabling the intentionally configured Ars Reactive crafting mechanic.

**Implementation-ready:** revise the authored preset manifest before creating a new shop expansion PR, and assert no `ars_nouveau:reactive` in all 28 presets; permanent shop stock still only seven iron items. No requested migration PR #531 edits, no full build/QA authorization.

## Owner correction — retain Farming for Blockheads Market as a specialist vendor (2026-11-22)

**Supersedes prior suggestion to retire the Market and duplicate every crop into Q Shop.** Keep the pinned `farming-for-blockheads` Market block and its native farming interface. Intended division:
- **Physical Market:** ordinary seeds/crop starters, saplings, fertilizers and curated spawn eggs (agricultural/husbandry focus); keep useful crop/animal equipment from the mod.
- **Q Shop:** prepared food, vanilla ore blocks and ordinary materials, equipment, enchantments, magical reagents, Relics/Artifacts and other adventurer supplies.
- **One underlying coin economy:** Market should ultimately be funded by the same **per-player virtual `coins`** earned from Q Shop/bounties, not require a separate independent emerald/diamond economic grind.

### Exact pinned source findings

- Farming for Blockheads pinned `farmingforblockheads-neoforge-1.21.1-21.1.14` branch `TwelveIterations/FarmingForBlockheads@1.21.1`. `MarketPresetRegistry`/Market data lets a datapack override `market_presets/*.json` to customize **physical item ingredient and count**. Sample `minecraft:animal_eggs` preset is **DISABLED** by default and uses **one diamond per egg** by default; must explicitly opt-in and rebalance, not silently turn on every spawn egg. Ars saplings/seeds presets use emeralds; normal default emerald payment can be overridden per preset.
- Source `MarketMenu` manages a real input payment slot and physically decrements the ItemStack in `onItemBought()`; `MarketBasketSlot.mayPickup` checks `isReadyToBuy()` using payment ingredient/count. Thus **datapack-only modification cannot debit virtual `coins` directly**. Do NOT falsely advertise `currency: 'coins'` in a Market recipe; its payment codec only supports `ingredient`, `count`, optional tooltip.
- Q Shop pinned 1.8.5 has a **virtual personal** `coins` wallet. `QShop.entry(...).buy(item).price(N, 'coins')` spends wallet coins to grant physical item; `.sell(item).price(N, 'coins')` consumes physical item and grants wallet coins. Official `CurrencyService.INSTANCE.getBalance/withdraw/deposit` API can also be called from Java add-ons, but does not automatically integrate with `MarketMenu` transactions.

### Minimal viable implementation, proposed

**Keep Market unchanged**, introduce a distinctive `tmm:market_token` physical item (or equivalent namespaced ID when registered) as the Market payment ingredient. Add Q Shop **two-way 1:1 exchange**, wallet coin ↔ one Market Token, with exact debit / exact grant, allowing surplus token redemption to wallet at parity. Replace/override market payment presets (via KubeJS datapack) for verified seed, sapling, fertilizer and egg entries, price costs in integer tokens, and keep original Market search/category UI and physical block.

**Security/economy constraints:** Token is never obtainable from recipes, natural loot, mob drops, direct vanilla emerald swaps, or other shops; explicitly exclude token from ProjectE EMC generation/transmutation, Replication and any copy/exchange pathways that could produce unlimited wallet currency. Don't allow infinite bidirectional mint loops; exchange must exactly consume or issue the token once, with no profit, and reject items altered or renamed as coin substitutes. Since a token is an item, confirm loss on death, storage, hopper automation etc. is acceptable; users can always reconvert unused tokens in Q Shop. No extra permanent *economic balance*: token is 1:1 representation of wallet coin, not a second bounty currency.

**Alternate future enhancement:** If owner requires **direct wallet payment in the Market with no token inventory or conversion**, implement a *server-authoritative* first-party Market/Q Shop adapter using `CurrencyService.withdraw` and an atomic output/grant transaction; Market's ordinary payment-slot flow must be replaced/hooked at every pickup/shift-click path.
